Subject: Subprocessor declaration for SMB pilot + export paths

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the quick demo last week — EmberTech is ready to start the 3-week SMB pilot the week of July 6. Before we kick off procurement needs a short subprocessor declaration so our legal team can confirm there are no export/import issues for our EU and APAC customers. Specifically, can you confirm:  

- A current roster of subprocessors that will process customer data for the pilot (names, primary function, country of processing).
- Any subprocessors that may transit or process data in APAC (we need to flag these for our local counsel).
- Whether any telemetry/observability vendors will receive raw tokens or only aggregated metrics.
- A short export-path diagram (high-level) showing where inference logs/telemetry and S3 backups may travel.
- A pointer to the exact DPA clause we should review for temporary third-party telemetry or analytics.

If you can send a spreadsheet + the diagram by Tuesday EOD (PDT) that would keep our procurement timeline on track. If there is an internal contact for security/compliance who should be copied, please include them.

Regards,
Aisha Khan
Legal Counsel, EmberTech
embertech-legal@embertech.com

--
Note: this request is limited to the SMB pilot scope (customer subset IDs will be provided once the roster is confirmed).

Subject: RE: Subprocessor declaration for SMB pilot + export paths

Hi team — sharing the initial roster and a few notes below. I attached a workbook (subprocessor_roster_v1.xlsx) and a one-page export-path diagram (export-path-diagram.png) to this thread. I also attached a short excerpt from the DPA that covers temporary telemetry recipients (DPA_addendum_excerpt.pdf).

Summary (pilot scope):
- Primary data processors for pilot: Redwood inference runtime (in-house), EdgeWave (edge caching partner, Singapore), Pulselytics (telemetry, aggregates + optional raw event sampling), and AWS S3 for backups (us-east-1 primary).
- APAC processing: EdgeWave (SG) will terminate some requests for latency-sensitive customers and will temporarily process ephemeral telemetry for health checks. Pulselytics may receive sampled raw events if sampling is enabled — we will mark that in the roster.
- Telemetry controls: by default Pulselytics receives only aggregated metrics. Raw event sampling is opt-in at the customer level and requires a DPA addendum acceptance.
- Export path: inference requests enter US-hosted inference clusters; cache misses may route to EdgeWave in SG (APAC) for a short tail; S3 backups remain in us-east but may be accessible by our ops engineers via a controlled VPN egress point. See diagram for arrows and retention windows.

Action items for EmberTech:
1) Confirm whether the pilot includes Australian customers (this will change cross-border notification).
2) If EmberTech requires no raw-event sampling, reply with "no-sampling" and we will disable sampling for the pilot by default.
3) If you need Pulselytics never to receive any sampled raw events, procurement & legal will need the signed DPA addendum (excerpt attached) before the pilot begins.

Notes for Redwood internal: Rishi — please confirm whether the ops VPN access requires any extra audit logs for this customer. Laura — once EmberTech confirms the scope, can procurement route the addendum through DocuSign?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com

Attachments referenced:
- subprocessor_roster_v1.xlsx (roster + flags)
- export-path-diagram.png (high-level)
- DPA_addendum_excerpt.pdf (telemetry addendum excerpt)

Aisha — thanks, attaching the files Kimberly prepared. Quick summary for your review:

- Roster: EdgeWave (edge cache, Singapore) and Pulselytics (telemetry, US) are the two subprocessors to note. EdgeWave will process ephemeral request bodies for cache purposes only when routing to APAC; Pulselytics receives aggregated metrics by default and sampled raw events only if the customer opts in.
- Export path: primary inference and backups remain US-hosted; EdgeWave introduces an APAC transit path for cache hits. Diagram attached.
- DPA: the attached excerpt shows the telemetry addendum language — if EmberTech requires a prohibition on raw-event sampling we will mark Pulselytics as "no raw event" and the addendum will be signed prior to pilot start.

Next steps: please reply with the two quick confirmations below by EOD Tue PDT so we can finalize procurement paperwork:  
1) Pilot includes Australian customers? (yes/no)
2) Sampling allowed for sampled raw events? (allow / disallow / allow-with-exclusions)

If you want a short call to walk through the diagram, Kimberly and I are available Tue 10:00–11:00 PDT.

Thanks again — looking forward to getting the pilot running.

Best,
